questions: When replacing every occurrence of x with y, does the replacement apply to the current state of S after previous operations, or only to the original S each time?
Is the operation allowed to choose x and y such that x equals y (a no-op)?
If a replacement creates new occurrences of a letter that was previously replaced, are those new occurrences also subject to later replacements?
Are we allowed to choose x and y such that y is a letter that already exists in the current S (potentially causing merges)?
Does the operation require that x and y be distinct letters?
Is the goal to make S identical to T exactly, or is it acceptable if S becomes T after all operations?
Can we choose x and y that are not present in the current S (e.g., replace a letter not in S)?
Should the minimum number of operations be computed over all possible sequences of replacements, including those that might temporarily make S non-matching intermediate states?
